items.title: Cursor details Fireworks key leak that led to malicious Claude Code extension
facts: An attacker obtained an access key Cursor had issued to Fireworks; the key was exposed by Fireworks and used to copy data from a read-only storage bucket containing limited coding agent traces, mostly from 2025, from sessions not in Privacy Mode.

Less than 0.01% of customers had API credentials exposed; the attacker used credentials from the traces to reach select SaaS tools and place malicious unauthorized copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on the marketplace cache.

At most 5,000 users who requested specific cached versions of Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 on October 29 potentially received the malicious build; Anthropic did not publish it and Open VSX never had the malware.

items.title: Claude Code Projects gains proactive coordinator, /btw and /fork support
facts: The coordinator is now much more proactive: it answers questions in the project chat and gives updates on the status of ongoing threads.
/btw and /fork now work inside projects; /btw spins off a side thread so the main thread stays on topic, and /fork starts a new thread from the current one.
Projects is in public beta for Pro and Max users; available on web, desktop and the latest mobile app.

items.title: Google Antigravity rolls out Dynamic Workflows with /run-workflow
facts: Use /run-workflow and the agent writes a Python script to orchestrate parallel and sequential subagents with structured handoffs.
The script gives deterministic control flow instead of prompt drift; review the script before it runs and save it to re-run the same flow anytime.
Primitives include phase(), parallel(), pipeline(), and agent() with per-agent model and workspace control.

items.title: Cloudflare open-sources Kitesurf browser engine for AI agents
facts: Kitesurf is open source on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license; it runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers, parses HTML, applies CSS, executes page JavaScript, and renders screenshots without a browser container.
It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), so you can connect clients such as Puppeteer.
You can run it locally or deploy your own instance to Cloudflare Workers; a Workers Paid plan is required for Dynamic Workers.

items.title: Developers discuss coordination overhead of parallel coding agents
facts: 5 agents working simultaneously doesn't mean 5x productivity; it can mean 5 sessions consuming limits, 5 branches to review, and merge conflicts when agents edit the same files.
Ask the coordinator to split into independent tasks, assign file ownership, and flag dependencies before running.

items.title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0 discussed for improving AI coding agents on web standards
facts: Google Chrome team released Modern Web Guidance 1.0 on 10 November as a set of skills that feeds coding agents web platform expertise, best practices and browser compatibility data.
At Japan's note inc., the pass rate on modern web controls rose from 61% to 94% across 180 runs on its production codebase when the prompt named it.

items.title: T3 Code gains theming features allowing Claude Code-like UI recreation
facts: User recreated Claude Code UI inside T3 Code using new theming features with Opus 5.5.
Preferred T3 Code functionality but previously returned to Claude Code for UI; now plans to stick with T3 Code.

items.title: cc-agent-brain provides local memory layer for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex
facts: cc-agent-brain gives Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex a local memory layer: SQLite with FTS5 retrieval, bi-temporal versioned memories, and full-session capture, all behind an MCP server.
Zero dependencies, Python, your machine only.

items.title: Claude Code desktop gains custom themes via mods
facts: You can now build custom themes for Claude Code on desktop with mods: change the colors, add an animated background, and make it your own.
Tell Claude how you want it to look, or get started with the theme-examples plugin.
